geometry.note: geometric envelope without gaps or keep-outs; says nothing about bonding, routing or thermal feasibility

interface_candidates_not_facts.note: 512 DQ at the repository's HBDRAM_500Mbps timing gives 8.192 TB/s per die, 2.4% above the stated 8

checks.check: aggregate channels as stated = dies x per die
aggregate capacity as stated = dies x per die
aggregate nominal bandwidth as stated = dies x per die
2 x 2 envelope fits the logic footprint (no gaps assumed)

banks_per_channel.note: every HBDRAM preset has one bank per channel (stated in the spec's docstring); 4 banks need a new preset

capacity_per_channel.note: 187.5 Mb (decimal) per channel: with a power-of-two DQ the rows x columns per bank are not an integer; read as GiB it is 192 Mib = 3 x 2^26 bits, which needs a non-power-of-two row count and a density the model has no tRFC / tREFI entry for. NOT rounded to a preset here.

timings.note: target timings / refresh unknown; HBDRAM_500Mbps / 400Mbps are the repository's, not the target's

four_domains.note: NPUsim has one [dram] endpoint and one staging link; four interface domains with local and cross-domain routes are not modeled. A single 1024-channel endpoint is an IDEALIZED aggregate-supply scenario only.

standin_runtime_probes.why: one die's channel count at 512 DQ x 500 Mbps (capacity 64 GB: NOT the target)
idealized single endpoint of all four dies (capacity 256 GB: NOT the target)
one die's channel count at 256 DQ (4.1 TB/s nominal: NOT the target rate)

decode_bound_example.note: arithmetic only, no model selected: a batch-1 decode token of a model whose weights fill W bytes reads W once; at the AGGREGATE THEORETICAL MAXIMUM that takes W / 32 TB/s. It is a lower bound on supply time, not a latency.
